source_caption:
Children of the Night (Les Enfants de la nuit, 2011) is a short French drama that tells a quiet, emotional story set during the final days of World War II. Directed by Caroline Deruas-Garrel and Olivier Berlemont, the film focuses on a young French girl who forms a fragile connection with a German soldier at a time when trust is dangerous and every decision carries weight.

The film is shot in black and white, giving it a soft, nostalgic feeling that makes the story feel like a memory from another time. Instead of focusing on battles or action, it stays close to small human moments, showing how fear, loneliness, and curiosity can bring people together even in the middle of war.

source_details.synopsis: Children of the Night is a 1985 American made-for-television drama film directed by Robert Markowitz. The film is a fictionalized biopic of Dr. Lois Lee, following her work among young prostitutes in Hollywood and the organization Children of the Night that she founded as a result.
